summary.en: A covert operation seized a Lockerbie bombing suspect on Libyan territory, showing continued security actions against international terrorism. Khalifa Haftar’s son met the Inspector General of Morocco’s Royal Armed Forces and later met Syria’s foreign minister in Libya, linking Libyan factions to regional actors. Over 130 migrants died when a boat capsized off the African coast, and mines under fire contest gold control in the Egypt-Sudan-Libya border triangle. The government warned of penalties for unauthorized protests, and there were two battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: En hemmelig operasjon tok en mistenkt i Lockerbie-bombingen på libysk territorium, og viser fortsatte sikkerhetstiltak mot internasjonal terrorisme. Khalifa Haftars sønn møtte inspektøren general for Marokkos kongelige væpnede styrker og møtte senere Syriens utenriksminister i Libya, og knytter libyske fraksjoner til regionale aktører. Over 130 migranter døde da en båt kantret utenfor den afrikanske kysten, og miner under ild strider om gullkontroll i trekanten ved grensen mellom Egypt, Sudan og Libya. Regjeringen advarte om straffer for uautoriserte protester, og det var to dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Libyan crisis
background.extract: The Libyan crisis is the current humanitarian crisis and political-military instability occurring in Libya, beginning with the Arab Spring protests of 2011, which led to two civil wars, foreign military intervention, and the ousting and killing of Muammar Gaddafi. The first civil war's aftermath and proliferation of armed groups led to violence and instability across the country, which erupted into renewed civil war in 2014. The second war lasted until 23 October 2020, when all parties agreed to a permanent ceasefire and negotiations.
